title: Angular PSF Glare: From Texture to Final Composite
abstract: How Version 24 builds a solid-angle-normalized PSF and turns sampled source luminance into screen-space glare.
imageAlt: Angular PSF components integrated into a normalized texture and accumulated as runtime glare
lede: This pipeline stores glare as angular density in sr⁻¹. Texture generation integrates four PSF components over each texel, normalizes their energy, and applies adaptation weights. Runtime sampling then converts area-light luminance into an additive glare result measured in cd/m².

sections.heading: Map texture space to visual angle
paragraphs: For texture resolution N, let H_tex = (N − 1) / 2 and θ_max = PSFMaxAngleDeg. A virtual focal length maps every center-relative texel position to an angle.

equations.label: Angle mapping
equations.expression:
f = H_tex / tan(θ_max)
r = √(x² + y²)
θ = atan(r / f) × 180° / π
terms: x and y are measured from the texture center. θ is measured in degrees.

equations.label: Texel solid angle
equations.expression:
J_Ω(x, y) = f / (f² + x² + y²)^(3/2)
Ω_texel = ∫_texel J_Ω(x, y) dxdy
terms: J_Ω is the solid-angle Jacobian of the virtual projection.

equations.label: Trapezoidal integration
equations.expression: E = Σ F(θ) × J_Ω × w_x × w_y × Δx × Δy
terms: The code uses 100 intervals near the center and 10 elsewhere.

sections.heading: Evaluate the PSF components
paragraphs: The texture combines a narrow core, two achromatic corona terms, and a spectral halo.

equations.label: Central core
terms: The narrow unscattered peak.

equations.label: Inner corona
terms: The fast-decaying inner glare.

equations.label: Outer corona
terms: The slower far-distance glare.

equations.label: Wavelength halo
terms: λ is measured in nanometres. The implementation samples 50 wavelengths from 400 nm to 700 nm.

sections.heading: Fade and normalize the component energy
paragraphs: The inner 40% of the circular texture is unchanged. A quintic fade removes the outer region before each component is normalized.

equations.label: Circular boundary
terms: Fade = 1 − S(t) for ρ < 1 and Fade = 0 for ρ ≥ 1.
The integrated component becomes E′_k = E_k × Fade.

equations.label: Scalar normalization
terms: Each scalar component sums to one.

equations.label: Halo normalization
terms: The colored component is normalized by total luminance.

sections.heading: Modulate the corona with radial lines
paragraphs: One-sided rays add structured streaks. Global and local normalization keep the raw mask mean near one before its contrast is reduced.

equations.label: Angular distance from a ray
equations.expression:
a = p · d
d_⊥ = |p_xd_y − p_yd_x|
δ = asin[d_⊥ / √(|p|² + f²)] × 180° / π
terms: A ray contributes only when a > 0.

equations.label: Line mask
equations.expression:
w_inner = 0.2w
Coverage = 1 − smoothstep(w_inner, w, δ)
M_raw(p) = Σ_j Coverage_j × RandomIntensity_j
terms: M(p) = lerp[1, clamp(M_raw(p), 0, 4), 0.25].

equations.label: Component modulation
equations.expression:
F₁ ← F₁M_corona
F₂ ← F₂M_corona
F₃ ← F₃M_halo
terms: F₁, F₂, and F₃ are normalized again after modulation.

equations.label: Density per steradian
terms: P has units sr⁻¹.

equations.label: Final texture
equations.expression:
Core = w₀P₀
Corona = w₁P₁ + w₂P₂
Halo_RGB = w₃P₃,RGB
terms: PSF_RGB = EnergyScale × [(Core + Corona)(1, 1, 1) + Halo_RGB].
The texture border is forced to black.

sections.heading: Sample each visible emitter
paragraphs: Each light uses N_s = PSFSourceSampleCount low-discrepancy samples. R_scaled and U_scaled use the same directional-candela scaling as the source pass.

equations.label: Sample sequence
terms: Rectangle: q = (2u − 1, 2v − 1).
Ellipse: q = √u(cos 2πv, sin 2πv).

equations.label: Sample position
terms: The sample lies inside the projected rectangle or ellipse.

sections.heading: Weight source luminance by emitter area
paragraphs: The source texture stores RGB luminance in cd/m². A shared luminance limit preserves color, then each sample is weighted by its share of the screen-space emitter.

equations.label: Screen-space emitter area
equations.expression:
A_axis = |R_xU_y − R_yU_x|
A_rectangle = 4A_axis
A_ellipse = πA_axis
A_sample = A_emitter / N_s
terms: A_axis is the parallelogram area of the two projected half-axes.

equations.label: Source-luminance limit
equations.expression:
L_max = max(L_R, L_G, L_B)
L_RGB ← L_RGB × PSFMaxIntensityCdM2 / L_max when L_max exceeds the limit
terms: All RGB channels use the same scale, preserving source color.

sections.heading: Preserve visual angle at runtime
paragraphs: The PSF footprint changes with projection and resolution so its apparent angular size remains approximately constant.

equations.label: Viewport-UV half-size
equations.expression:
h_u = 0.5 × tan(α) × P_x
h_v = 0.5 × tan(α) × P_y
terms: α is PSFGeneratedMaxAngleDeg. P_x and P_y are projection-matrix scales.

equations.label: Destination-pixel solid angle
terms: W_view and H_view are viewport dimensions. Ω_pixel is measured in sr.

sections.heading: Accumulate and composite the glare
paragraphs: Every source sample contributes physical glare to each covered pixel. All samples and visible lights are added into a render target measured in cd/m².

equations.label: Per-sample contribution
terms: L_PSF,p = Σ_lights Σ_samples ΔL_i,p.

equations.label: Final composite
terms: The source brightness is not removed or redistributed.

references.label: Spencer et al., Physically-Based Glare Effects for Digital Images (1995)
DOI: Physically-Based Glare Effects for Digital Images

closing: Version 24 carries one unit-consistent path from angular PSF energy to an additive glare image: integrate in solid angle, store density in sr⁻¹, then accumulate area-weighted source luminance in cd/m².
